intro: Your Balance (KCAL Analytics) turns honest logs into a personal energy picture: what is working, what the records support, and what is still unknown. kCal Assistant writes the review; kCal Buddy stays your everyday food companion.
buddyTip: Open Your Balance from Home → Log → My Shortcuts when you want the connected picture — food, movement and recovery — not a verdict on a single morning weigh-in.
mission: Open Your Balance, save or skip the starting-point questions, and leave with one routine to keep or one small next step.
why: Without a connected review, Foodiary is a pile of receipts. Your Balance shows whether energy, protein, movement and sleep are working under real life.
A saved calorie target is not proof that a different number is excessive. Estimated burn, the saved target and any proposed plan stay separate.
Incomplete logging cannot establish actual intake or inactivity. Missing a dinner label does not prove an incomplete day.
Successful routines deserve to be kept. The review will not invent a harder goal just to fill a report.

points: Your Balance card in My Shortcuts (Home → Log). It is not a second Home tile.
Starting-point questions you can skip or edit later
Your energy — readiness, windows and provenance
Your patterns — descriptive evidence, not causes
Your next step — one primary action or a routine to keep

misconceptions.myth: Opening Your Balance spends AI credits.
misconceptions.truth: Opening Your Balance only reaches setup. Generation is a later explicit action with a real receipt.

misconceptions.myth: Fourteen weigh-in rows always mean two weeks.
misconceptions.truth: Row count is not calendar duration. Your Balance labels both the review window and the longer baseline evidence window.

how.lead: Make Your Balance a calm appointment.
steps: Keep ordinary meals and weigh-ins on Home
Open Home → Log → My Shortcuts → Your Balance
Answer how the routine feels, or skip
Read Your energy before changing a target
Keep a working routine when the records agree
Rate whether the review was useful — that is not a health outcome
how.buddyHelps: Buddy capture feeds the diary that Your Balance reads. Coaching quality rises when trends reflect real restaurants, travel, and training — not curated highlights.

sections.title: Your energy
paras: Readiness is owned by the existing Method gate: food days, weigh-ins on different days, and the calendar span of those records. Copy shows have/need and either Requirement met or remaining days — never a duplicated unit. Reaching a count does not guarantee a stable personal calibration. A saved review stays frozen; session complete/incomplete marks are not written into that report.

sections.title: Your patterns
paras: Findings stay descriptive. Planned training is not completed training. Missing movement is not proven inactivity. General mood is not timed fatigue.

sections.title: Applying a target
paras: A proposed number is not applied until you edit the existing goal. Hockey season does not add calories automatically.

mistakes.quote: I judged my whole program on this morning’s weigh-in.
mistakes.why: Use the review window. One morning is weather, not climate.

mistakes.quote: Progress looked bad so I deleted old logs.
mistakes.why: Deleting erases learning. Keep honesty; adjust forward.

mistakes.quote: I only open this when I feel guilty.
mistakes.why: Scheduled calm reviews beat shame-triggered chart spirals.

encouragement: Your Balance is a mirror for patterns, not a verdict on your worth. Log honestly, review when you want the connected picture, keep what works.
